licences.sdpra: CC BY 4.0. The SDPRA-2021 shared-task data (Reddy & Saini, Mendeley Data doi:10.17632/njb74czv49.1, version 1; public zip sha256 0fee9f8e...) is CC BY 4.0. SciPrompt's 'test' is a 10% re-split of the shared task's train+validation (16,800 + 11,200 = 28,000 = 25,200 + 2,800); all 2,800 test rows were matched to a Mendeley train/validation row with the same label after alphanumeric normalisation (2,354 match after whitespace normalisation alone; the rest differ only in removed backslashes). Abstracts are frozen verbatim with attribution.

test_n_resolution.arxiv: Release 5,300 = 53 x 100 (paper Table 5, Appendix B '100 samples for each category as test set'). Paper's 30-SciBERT-token filter drops 0 (paper: test 5,300). Minus 5 non-English -> 5,295.
test_n_resolution.s2orc: Release 5,700 = 19 x 300 (Table 5, file name 300_random_sample). Filter drops 0 (paper: 5,700). Minus 40 non-English -> 5,660.
test_n_resolution.sdpra: Release 2,800 (Table 5 gives 2,800). The paper's evaluated test set is 2,790 (Appendix B, p. 6099: 'abstracts shorter than 30 tokens were excluded ... 2,790 for SDPRA'); recomputing sdpra_script.py's filter (BertTokenizer allenai/scibert_scivocab_uncased@24f92d32, transformers 4.38.1, len(input_ids) < 30) drops exactly 10 rows (840, 1111, 1125, 1544, 1683, 1725, 2183, 2283, 2530, 2791; e.g. 'This paper has been withdrawn'), reproducing 2,790. Minus 1 non-English -> 2,789.
test_n_resolution.emerging_nlp: Release 420 = 21 x 20 (Table 5; Section 5.2: 30 per topic, 5 train + 5 validation, rest test). Filter drops 0. No non-English rows -> 420. 3 abstracts occur twice with the same label (rows 22/25, 156/157, 192/199); kept as released.

english_verification.paper: Section 4.1: 'three publicly available datasets in English'; Emerging NLP collected from arXiv cs.CL. S2ORC abstracts come from Semantic Scholar without a language filter.
english_verification.method: All 14,220 release test abstracts: (1) langid.py 1.1.6 on each whole abstract; (2) langid (normalised probabilities) on every sentence of >= 8 words, flag non-en with p > 0.99; (3) count of common Spanish/French/German/Portuguese/Italian function words; (4) non-Latin letter count >= 5 and any run of >= 3 Cyrillic/Hebrew/Arabic/Thai/CJK/Hangul characters; (5) foreign 'abstract/keywords' headings (Resumen, Résumé, Özet, Kata kunci, 关键词, ...); (6) Latin-diacritic density > 1%. 281 candidates; each was read (text only, no labels or Jev output).
english_verification.rule: Exclude an abstract containing any non-English sentence, clause or multi-word phrase: parallel translations, foreign keyword lines, publisher notices (same rule as EZ-STANCE). Keep English abstracts whose only non-English material is proper names, cited titles (e.g. German/Italian/French book titles in reviews), single glossed terms in any script (e.g. Chinese characters after romanised terms), OCR-spaced English, mojibake punctuation, and a name-only author list (s2orc 5509).
english_verification.result: 46 excluded: arXiv 5 (English abstracts followed by French/Spanish/Polish/German translations), SDPRA 1 (English + French), S2ORC 40 (Japanese, Russian, Ukrainian, Turkish, Spanish, Catalan, Portuguese, French, Italian, Romanian, Polish, Lithuanian, Finnish, Swedish, Thai, Chinese, Indonesian text or keyword lines), Emerging NLP 0. List with per-row notes: data/frozen/sciprompt/excluded.jsonl (reason non_english) and NON_ENGLISH in scripts/prepare_sciprompt.py.
english_verification.per_label_effect: arXiv: math.LO, physics.class-ph, math.MG, cs.DS, cs.LG 99 each (others 100). S2ORC: Art 291, Philosophy 293, Political Science 295, Geography 296, Psychology 297, Economics/Biology/Engineering/Geology 298, Environmental Science/Materials Science/Business/Sociology 299, others 300. SDPRA (after the paper filter and 1 non-English): CL 484, CR 471, NI 449, DS 413, DC 351, SE 322, LO 299 (release 485/474/450/417/352/322/300).

frozen.builder: scripts/prepare_sciprompt.py (asserts the zip SHA-256, release N per dataset, and that the recomputed short-abstract filter equals the frozen list)
frozen.format: JSONL per dataset: id (sciprompt-<dataset>-test-<release row>), row (0-based release row), gold (release label: arXiv code, S2 field name, SDPRA code, Emerging NLP class name), sha256 = SHA-256 of compact JSON [abstract, gold] (UTF-8); sdpra and emerging_nlp rows also carry the abstract. Abstract = the string the paper's loader feeds the model (line files: stripped line; CSV: raw field). items() rebuilds arXiv/S2ORC text from the zip and checks every hash.

data_notes: Train/test overlap in the release (irrelevant to zero-shot Jev, favours the paper's few-shot/full fine-tuned models only marginally): identical abstracts in train and test: arXiv 14, S2ORC 152, SDPRA 2, Emerging NLP 6.
The same V2V channel-model abstract appears in arXiv (row 730, cs.NI) and SDPRA (row 2359, NI).

S2ORC contains noisy Semantic Scholar 'abstracts' kept as released: book-review openings, reference lists, figure captions, retraction notices, 10,000-char truncated full texts (5 rows at exactly 10,000 chars).

Truncation rule (frozen in sciprompt.py): abstract cut to 60,000 chars; the longest frozen abstract is 10,000 chars, so 0 items are truncated. Largest request: arXiv question (~3.5K tokens) + abstract.
deviations: Non-English abstracts excluded (English-only rule): scored N arXiv 5,295 (paper 5,300), S2ORC 5,660 (5,700), SDPRA 2,789 (2,790), Emerging NLP 420 (420). Paper numbers are on the full sets.
SDPRA N follows the paper's evaluated set (2,790 after its 30-token filter) rather than Table 5's 2,800 (pre-filter count); the filter is the paper's own code, recomputed, not re-tuned.

arXiv and SDPRA options use arXiv's official category names/descriptions (SDPRA: shared-task names) instead of the paper's lower-case field words, because two of the paper's words name the wrong category (math.AP 'applied mathematics' is Analysis of PDEs; cs.CY 'cryptography and security' is Computers and Society, while cs.CR is 'cryptography'). The paper's words are kept in each prompt's _paper_field_words.
Jev is zero-shot; the matching comparison is paper Table 2 (zero-shot) and Figure 3 lower panel (Emerging NLP zero-shot). Few-shot numbers (Table 1, Figure 3 upper) are reported for context only.
